events.text:
**Recommendation:** Go to Muskegon. Grand Haven is a close second and St. Joseph is a fair third. Troll spoons 35–90 ft down over 120–200 ft of water. The newest reports are 6 days old (2022-05-18), and no wind forecast came back, so check the marine forecast before you launch.

| Port | My rating (0–4) | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Muskegon | 3 (good) | Reported good |
| Grand Haven | 3 (good) | Reported good |
| St. Joseph | 3 (good), but mostly coho | Good for coho, weak for Chinook |
| South Haven | 2 (average) | Reported fair |

**What the reports say**
- **Muskegon:** "Boats were doing well" on salmon 35–90 ft down in 120–200 ft of water. Green and blue spoons and white flies worked well, and a few fish came on meat rigs (Muskegon, 2022-05-18). Quality was 3.
- **Grand Haven:** "Salmon action was good" 30–120 ft down in 130–240 ft of water (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18). Quality was 3, but no lures were named. Two weeks earlier boats were in only 30–60 ft, catching Chinook and a few coho (Grand Haven, 2022-05-04). The fish have moved deeper since.
- **St. Joseph:**
  - Boat fishing was good (quality 3), on spoons, from 40 ft to well past 120 ft of water (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18).
  - The catch was mostly coho and steelhead. Chinook were few (quality 1) and lake trout were mixed in (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18).
  - No fish depth was given.
- **South Haven:** Fishing was "fair" (quality 2). Fish were "spread out from 30 feet of water to deeper depths," and most boats trolled spoons (South Haven, 2022-05-18). It was also slow on 05-04, and the reports mention no specific depth or lure.

**Water:** The buoy-measured surface temperature for the week before today averaged about 52 F at Muskegon and Grand Haven. It averaged about 53 F at South Haven and St. Joseph. All four ports fell 3–4 F over that week (current conditions, 2022-05-24). I had no modeled cold-layer depth or wind forecast.

**My read**
- I'd expect the north ports to stay ahead. They had the most consistent "good" reports, and both showed fish well offshore and well down.
- Surface water of 52–53 F is inside the 52–58 F range Chinook and coho prefer (NY DEC, general guidance). I'd expect fish to be spread through the water column, so start around 35–60 ft and adjust until you find the marks.
- The 3–4 F drop this week may mean cold water has come up along the shore. That could shift fish, so be ready to move shallower or deeper than last week's depths.
- South Haven's rating is held down by its vague, weaker report, not by evidence that it's bad.

**Caveats**
- The newest report is 6 days old, and late May conditions change quickly.
- The same-season history search returned only this year's reports, so I have no earlier seasons to compare.
- Each port's rating is based on one report from 2022-05-18, so treat them as rough.

**Sources**
- 2022-05-18 (all four ports): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3186585
- 2022-05-04: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
